transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I've been having this issue when people are talking to me. Like, people at the museum will be talking right to me about the next art walk, and I’ll be looking right at them, but then... I realize I completely missed the middle of what they just said. I always end up having to ask them to run it by me again. It's just been happening enough lately that I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Do you have any trouble hearing other people speak?
No, my hearing is fine. I don't have any trouble actually hearing the words they're saying. It's more like my brain just stops paying attention to them for a minute.
Have you had this kind of trouble paying attention since you were a child?

Yes, actually, I have. Even back in grade school, I remember my report cards always said things like "daydreams a lot" or "needs reminders to finish work." And my mother... she used to have to sit right beside me while I did my homework, just to keep me on track. That was definitely before I was twelve, so yeah, it's been going on for a long time.
Do you often feel restless or have a hard time sitting still?
No, not really. I don't feel restless, and sitting still isn't really a problem for me. I can sit in one spot for a long time without feeling like I need to move around.
Do you often interrupt people or blurt out answers before they’ve finished asking the question?

No, I don't really do that. I usually just let people finish what they're saying. If anything, I'm probably just sitting there quiet because my mind is drifting off somewhere else, but I don't interrupt them or blurt things out.
Do you remember these attention problems starting before you were 12 years old?

Yeah, like I mentioned just a minute ago, I definitely do. It was well before I was twelve. Back in grade school, my report cards always had those notes saying I daydreamed or needed reminders to finish my work. And my mother having to sit right beside me to keep me on track with my homework... all of that was happening when I was just a young kid, definitely before twelve.
Do these attention problems cause you trouble in more than one part of your life, like work or school and also at home?

Well, I'm not working these days, so work isn't really a factor for me anymore. And at home... I don't know, I wouldn't say it causes me any real trouble. I mean, I get distracted, sure, but it's not causing major problems across my life or anything. So, no, I haven't really noticed it being an issue like that.
Do these attention problems make it hard for you to do everyday tasks reliably?

Well, it does affect some things I do. I volunteer with a museum group, and... lately, they've had to quietly shift some of the planning pieces away from me because I just wasn't keeping track of it all. And I used to lead these art walks, but I've stopped feeling confident doing it the way I used to. It just gets too hard to keep everything straight.
Have you noticed that your concentration or memory has gotten worse compared with how it used to be?

No, I wouldn't say it's gotten worse. I mean... it's pretty much always been this way for me. Like I was saying about when I was a kid, I've always been a bit scattered. So, no, I haven't really noticed any big decline or anything as I've gotten older. It's just the same as it's always been.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory?

Not really, no. My memory itself is... it's fine, I think. I mean, if I'm actually paying attention to something, I remember it just fine. It's more just getting distracted or losing track of what I'm doing in the moment, like I was saying before. But as far as actual memory problems go, no, I haven't noticed anything like that.
Do these attention problems cause trouble in more than one part of your life, such as home and social situations?

Well, yeah, I'd say so. Like I mentioned, it definitely affects my volunteer work at the museum. But it happens at home, too. I'll start a chore, like doing the laundry, and then... I don't know, I'll go to the kitchen for a glass of water, see the mail, start sorting that, and completely forget about the laundry for the rest of the day. And socially, it can be tough to follow conversations if there's a lot going on around me. So, yes, it definitely pops up in a few different areas of my life.
Have you been told by anyone close to you that your attention or memory has gotten noticeably worse in recent months or years?

No, nobody's said anything like that to me. My wife gets frustrated with me sometimes for leaving things half-done, but she hasn't said it's getting worse. It's just the same stuff she's always gotten onto me about. So, no, no one has mentioned any recent changes or anything getting worse.
